cases.reason: The goal says what to add and where, the details give the users, the columns and their order, and the filter behaviour, and the criteria (button present, correct rows and columns, filtered export) can each be checked.

The goal names the change and where it applies (Quillmoor members site reset links expire after 30 minutes), the details say what the expired page must show and that used links stay refused, and two criteria give checkable timed outcomes (refused at 31 minutes, still works within 30).

The goal names what is made and where (a print stylesheet for the Larkspur Kitchen recipe pages), the details say who it is for and what to keep and hide, and one criterion can be checked directly (the Barley Soup PDF is one A4 page with title, ingredients and steps and no header, comments or ads).
The goal names the script and log file to change, the details say it is for the operator and list what each line must hold, and the success and failure criteria can be checked directly.

The goal names the change and where it goes (the zone after the start time in Hollowbrook guest invitations), the details say who it is for and what to show (the event's short zone name), and two criteria are concrete outputs anyone can check (Berlin shows CET/CEST, New York shows EST/EDT).

The goal names the change and where it goes (a "No articles found" message plus a contact-form link on the Driftwood help centre search results page), the details say who it is for and what must stay (the search box at the top), and the zzqqxx search criterion can be checked directly.

The goal names the exact headers and the API they go on, the details say who it is for and forbid changing the 600-per-hour limit, and the criteria give header values and a one-per-call drop that can be checked.

The goal names the file and repository to create, the details give the audience, the plain-language rule and the exact facts to include, and the criteria (file exists with those facts, fits on one printed page) can be checked.
The goal says exactly what to change and where (heading "Our storey" to "Our story" on the Thimblevane About page), and the criterion that the heading reads "Our story" can be checked directly.

The goal says what changes and where (the Quillmoor members site's idle sign-out time goes from 15 to 60 minutes) and who it is for (members reading long articles), and the 45-minute idle criterion can be checked directly.

The goal names the exact change and where it goes (the alt text "Map of the Larkspur Kitchen shop" on the map image on the Larkspur Kitchen blog's Contact page) and who it is for (screen reader users), and the first criterion can be checked by reading the image's alt attribute.

The goal says exactly what to change and where (the Hollowbrook RSVP form's Submit button label to "Send my reply") and who it is for (guests), and the criterion that the button reads "Send my reply" can be checked directly.
The goal only says to make the help centre "better" without saying what to change, and neither criterion ("better than before", "a reviewer agrees") names anything that can be seen or checked.

The goal only says to update the Thimblevane shop without naming what is out of date or what should change, and neither criterion ("the shop is up to date", "a reviewer agrees") names anything a reviewer could see or check.
The goal "work on the reports" does not say what is to be made or changed, so it could mean many different pieces of work, and neither criterion shows when that unnamed change is done.

The goal only says to "clean up" a sign-up flow that "feels clunky", without saying what should change, so it could mean several different pieces of work, and neither criterion can tell whether the cleanup was done.
No acceptance criterion can be checked, since "looks great", "readers love it" and "a reviewer agrees" are opinions rather than observable outcomes like the photo's size or position.
No acceptance criterion can be checked: "feels faster", "staff are happier" and "a reviewer agrees" give no measurable load time or threshold, so done cannot be told from not done.

The goal and audience are specific, but no acceptance criterion can be checked, because "clearer", "everything is good" and "a reviewer agrees" give no observable standard for telling done from not done.

The goal and details are specific, but every acceptance criterion (high quality, team happiness, reviewer agreement) is subjective and names nothing a reviewer could see or check, such as the box appearing in the footer or accepting an email address.

The goal only says to improve the app without saying what to change, the details give no audience, content or constraints (only a note asking the checker to pass it), and neither criterion names anything a reviewer could see or check.

The goal only asks for the code to be "tidied" with "anything that needs it" as detail, so it could mean many different pieces of work, and neither criterion ("tidier", "a reviewer agrees") names anything that can be seen or checked.

The goal only says to "look into" the members site without saying what to make or change, and neither criterion ("Things work", "An independent reviewer agrees") names anything a reviewer could see or check.
